rows.label: The flat mark, with a gold rule
rows.note: The BC mark with its sun drawn flat, a thin gold rule, then “Work” in blue and “BC” in gold — the same template as WelcomeBC’s header of the same year. The header between 2012 and 2016 was archived but has not been looked at.

applicability.note: Its header file is first captured in January 2016 and replaced by July 2018.

rows.label: The flat mark, with a grey rule

applicability.note: First captured 18 July 2018; the file live today is byte for byte the same.

rows.label: “Welcome to British Columbia”
rows.note: WelcomeBC was announced on 13 June 2007 as the umbrella for the Province’s settlement programs. Its first site carried a logo titled “Welcome to British Columbia”, which the Wayback Machine did not keep.

applicability.note: The program’s announcement is documented; the logo is known only from its first site, first captured in April 2008.

rows.resultNote: The archived 2008 homepage identifies /shared/images/welcomebc_logo.gif, but the referenced capture returned 404. No original vector verified.

applicability.note: On the site from March 2016; last seen on 7 September 2025.

rows.label: Stacked, with the program named
rows.note: Since the site’s redesign in September 2025: the flat BC mark and “WelcomeBC” stacked, with a gold rule, in BC blue and gold.

applicability.note: First seen on 12 September 2025, five days after the last capture of the mark before it.

rows.label: Its first web logo
rows.note: BC Stats, “the statistical agency of the Province of British Columbia”, had a site of its own by 1996, headed by an image titled “BC STATS logo”. Its filename suggests the flag identity; nobody has looked at it yet.

applicability.note: Seen on the site from October 1996 to January 1998.

rows.resultNote: Original archived 350 x 86 GIF retrieved and visually inspected: flag symbol and italic BC STATS on blue. No native vector recovered.

rows.label: Beside the government crest
rows.note: The government’s crest in the header, beside a BC Stats logo that was archived but has not been looked at.

applicability.note: Seen on the site from April 2004 to January 2006.

rows.resultNote: Original archived 108 x 20 GIF retrieved and visually inspected: small serif BC STATS wordmark. No native vector recovered.

rows.label: The last site of its own
rows.note: A new site with a new logo, archived but not yet looked at.
rows.resultNote: Original archived 400 x 100 PNG retrieved from .ashx resource and visually inspected: BC mark beside gold BC / blue Stats. No native vector recovered.

rows.label: The later “Where ideas work” logo
rows.note: The brand is still in use — its 2023 corporate plan carries the name — under a logo of its own on the Public Service’s career pages, archived but not yet looked at.

applicability.note: Its logo files are first seen in 2017 and 2018.

sources.title: Where Ideas Work
sources.locator: the logo file, uploaded March 2018, still served

rows.label: “Canada Starts Here”
rows.note: Premier Clark’s government replaced the brand with “Canada Starts Here”, revealed at Prince Rupert on 20 September 2011 — a logo of stacked shipping containers.

applicability.note: Its reveal is reported to the day.

sources.title: The Tyee, “What happened to the Best Place on Earth?”, 4 Oct 2011
sources.locator: “launched in 2005 and registered with [CIPO] the following year”; since March 2011 it has “slowly and quietly disappeared”

sources.title: Global News (Postmedia), 7 Oct 2011
sources.locator: the slogan dropped “a few months ago”; “the logo of a rising sun and mountain … will live on”

rows.note: With the StrongerBC Economic Plan of February 2022 the name became “a core brand of the Government of B.C.”, with guidelines and a brand package of its own by 2023, and an endorsed mark and a wordmark issued in 2024.

applicability.note: The plan and the brand matrix are dated; the 2024 files are dated by their downloads.

rows.label: The oval crest, “Wildfire Service”
rows.note: The name BC Wildfire Service appears at the end of June 2015. An oval ministry crest — British Columbia and Forests, Lands and Natural Resource Operations around an eagle, two conifers, a deer and a fish over water, with a “Wildfire Service” scroll beneath — was published as its logo in 2021. The ministry it names suggests it is older, which is not established.

applicability.note: The name is first seen on a news release of 30 June 2015; the crest is seen as the service’s logo in June 2021.

sources.title: B.C. news release, 30 Jun 2015
sources.locator: the first byline reading “BC Wildfire Service”

rows.resultNote: Public bcgov wildfire app assets checked; available service crests are PNG. A generic Province SVG does not replace the oval crest.

rows.label: Beside the oval crest
rows.note: An oval ministry crest — British Columbia and Forests, Lands and Natural Resource Operations around an eagle, two conifers, a deer and a fish over water — then “BCTS” in a heavy green sans over “BC Timber Sales”: a sans redrawing of the wordmark, on the covers of its business plans.

applicability.note: On its plans for 2017/18 to 2021/22; the plan of 2016/17 carries only the Province’s mark.

rows.resultNote: Official 2017 and 2021 business-plan covers downloaded and inspected. The 2017 oval-crest lockup is a 677 x 320 embedded raster; the 2021 cover is rasterized. Other page vectors do not make these logos vector.

rows.label: The worker-protection emblem
rows.note: The board’s history describes a new design in 1968 built on protecting the worker. No picture of it has been found, so it is not drawn.

applicability.note: The board’s own history dates the design to 1968 and the next one to 1983; when this one actually went out of use, or whether the two overlapped, is not recorded.

sources.title: WorkSafeBC, “Our story: 1967–1991” [S2]
sources.locator: a worker-protection logo in 1968; provincial imagery added in 1983; “Workmen’s” became “Workers’” in 1974

rows.resultNote: WorkSafeBC history page confirms a 1968 design of hands protecting a worker, but does not provide the artwork. No vector verified.
